text:
cs-team: FYI customer AcmeAds reporting p99 gen latency ~2.1s on dedicated-usw2 after the weekend driver/kernel updates. low error rate but tail latency up, customer SLA complaining. timeline: spike ~03:05 UTC, persisted ~20m.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-1123 — paging oncall.

oncall: On it. Pulling metrics and recent deploys. Correlating with driver rollout window.

devon: Correlation looks strong. NVMe avgq-sz jumped on affected hosts. quick iostat snapshot from 03:12: 
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device        r/s   w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1       120   10   5000   200      45.0      12.3    2.1   0.83  99.9
```
Looks like host io saturation under tail workloads.

maya: Seeing repeated nvme qpair timeouts in dmesg around same time: `nvme0: qpair 3 submit timeout` and `nvme0n1: abort command` entries.

jess: KV cache miss-rate spiked too — prefix cache warmups blocked by slow backend IO. p95 mostly fine, p99 is where customers feel it.

sam: Initial hypothesis: new NVMe driver + kernel irq affinity change + GPU driver update shifted interrupt patterns; under mixed GPU+IO, latency amplifies. Repro on canary with kernel 6.1 + driver 535.12.

liam: Immediate mitigations I recommend: 1) route Acme traffic to fallback pool running older driver, 2) reduce sequence length/model variant for heavy tails to reduce IO, 3) apply blkio throttling on noisy hosts. Example throttle: `echo 1024 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/<group>/blkio.weight`.

oncall: Routing to fallback-dedicated-usw2-old-driver now (draining 4 pods). Applying cgroup blkio throttle on 6 nodes in affected rack.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered: driver rollback job started for dedicated-usw2-canary (4 hosts). Watch logs: /var/log/drivers/rollback.log

devon: Early numbers are promising — Acme p99 dropped from ~2.1s -> ~700ms after routing. Still monitoring for noise.

maya: Long-term fixes: coordinate vendor on NVMe firmware, verify irq/coalescing defaults, consider qdisc and io_uring paths for heavy tail ops, and add a KV cache prewarm step during pod start to reduce cold IO.

cs-team: I'll draft a customer update: short summary + current mitigation + ETA to confirm rollback. CC @account-team.

sam: Follow-ups: open a postmortem, include reproducer steps: `fio --name=randread --rw=randread --bs=128k --iodepth=64 --numjobs=4 --runtime=60` while generating synthetic GPU load. Attach perf traces and nvme logs.

liam: File vendor bug with perf trace: `perf record -a -g -- sleep 30` + nvme diag logs. Also recommend we add an automated qdepth alert.

jess: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

cs-team: Will keep thread updated with rollback completion and customer confirm.
